intro: Most commands are accessible from the command palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS, `Ctrl+Shift+P` on Windows/Linux). Type **xcaffold** to filter to extension commands. A small number of commands are wired to sidebar toolbar buttons and are noted below.

categories.name: Lifecycle Commands
categories.description: These commands map directly to xcaffold CLI operations and run against the workspace root.

descriptions.xcaffold.validate: Check all manifests for schema and cross-reference errors
descriptions.xcaffold.status: Show compilation state and detect drift
descriptions.xcaffold.graph: Open the interactive D3 dependency graph

categories.name: Editor Commands
categories.description: These commands operate on the file currently open in the active editor or on resources selected in the tree view.

descriptions.xcaffold.openResource: Open a resource's source file from tree view
descriptions.xcaffold.findReferences: Find all files referencing a resource
descriptions.xcaffold.newResource: Create a new `.xcaf` resource from template (opens a dialog)
descriptions.xcaffold.deleteResource: Remove a resource and its file
descriptions.xcaffold.refreshExplorer: Refresh the resource tree view (also the refresh toolbar button on the Resource Explorer sidebar)

categories.name: Wizard Commands
categories.description: Guided, multi-step commands that walk through a workflow interactively.

categories.name: Webview Commands
categories.description: These commands open dedicated panels inside VS Code.

descriptions.xcaffold.refreshDashboard: Refresh the status dashboard data (also the refresh toolbar button on the Status Dashboard sidebar)

outro:
Most commands require the xcaffold CLI to be installed and available on `PATH`. The exceptions are file and tree operations (Open File, Find References, New Resource, Delete Resource, Refresh Explorer) which work without the CLI. If the CLI is not found, commands that need it will display a "CLI not found" notification with a link to the installation guide.

See [Getting Started](getting-started.md#troubleshooting) for CLI path configuration.
